change: Board 376: page, session and impression rates become three metrics, and a bare RPM header is refused rather than guessed at
_context: WHY THIS WAS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A THEORETICAL ONE.
['rpm', ['rpm', 'pagerpm', 'sessionrpm', 'ecpm']],
One metric, four synonyms. mapHeaders keeps the FIRST match and skips the
rest, so which column won was decided by its POSITION IN THE FILE rather
than by what it meant. lib/class-monetization.js multiplies the rpm metric
by PAGEVIEWS, so a session rate landing there overstates every class revenue
figure by pages-per-session.
Measured, not argued: on Raptive's own export for 2026-08-14 to 09-12, whose
own arithmetic reconciles on all 30 rows, the page rate averaged $7.20 and
the session rate $21.42. A factor of 2.97, with pages per session at 2.82,
which is the same number from the other side.
Raptive puts 'Page RPM' to the LEFT of 'RPM', so importing the real export
was correct by luck. The fix is a split rather than a reorder, because a
reorder keeps the luck and merely makes it slightly better luck.
A BARE rpm IS REFUSED, not assigned to a best guess. Raptive's bare column
is the SESSION rate, so either mapping would be wrong for some vendor. The
column is reported in ambiguous_headers with both readings and the remedy,
and no value is stored, which leaves the model reporting null. That is the
safe direction: a missing reading is recoverable and a wrong one looks right.
TWO MUTATIONS WERE REMOVED FROM THE BATTERY rather than kept, and the reason
is recorded in the harness. Adding a bare rpm back into either HEADER_MAP
list is INERT, because AMBIGUOUS is consulted first and returns before the
map is reached. Both left the suite green, which reads as an unguarded rule
and is in fact defence in depth working. The ORDERING is what makes them
inert, so the ordering is what gets mutated instead, and that one does go
red. A mutation that cannot fail is not a test.
NO live CHECK, and a CORRECTION. The first draft of this manifest said no
rederive was available either, and ran on suite plus mutation. The gate refused
it, correctly: two kinds is not three, and suite plus mutation is only this repo
talking to itself. The refusal was right and the note was wrong.
A rederive was available and is the honest kind here. scripts/
rederive-rate-denominators.js never reads a column heading. For every rate a
parse stored it recomputes all three candidates from the RAW revenue and
denominator columns and asks which one the number actually satisfies, so a value
stored under a metric whose arithmetic it does not match is the defect whatever
the column was called. It also PERMUTES the rate columns through all six
orderings, because a single hand-written order is what hid the bug.
Confirmed against the pre-fix state rather than assumed: with the collision and
the refusal both removed, the re-derivation goes red on 3 of its 6 assertions,
including the board 376 defect itself. One assertion still PASSES there, and
that is instructive: on Raptive's real column order the page rate happens to
win, which is the 'correct by luck' case. Only the permutation assertion sees
the general failure.
The live half stays unavailable: this is import-path only and POST
/api/admin/traffic/import is fail closed, so nothing is observable without the
admin key. A sha pin would be a dated receipt, per the 2026-09-18 note.
